rules.passEvidence: Recovered {n} words of text.
rules.failEvidence: Only {n} {n|word|words} of text could be recovered.
rules.fix: Save the resume as a text-based PDF rather than a scan or an image.

rules.passEvidence: An email address was found.
rules.failEvidence: No email address was found.
rules.fix: Add an email address at the top of the first page, as plain text in the body rather than in a page header.

rules.passEvidence: Contact details appear near the top of the document.
rules.failEvidence: Contact details appear well below the top of the document.
rules.fix: Put the email address and phone number at the top of the first page, in the body of the document rather than in a page header, which many ATS parsers skip.

rules.passEvidence: An experience section heading was found.
rules.failEvidence: No experience section heading was found.
rules.fix: Add a heading reading 'Experience' above the work history.

rules.passEvidence: An education section heading was found.
rules.failEvidence: No education section heading was found.
rules.fix: Add a heading reading 'Education' above the qualifications.

rules.passEvidence: A skills section heading was found.
rules.failEvidence: No skills section heading was found.
rules.fix: Add a heading reading 'Skills' above the skills list.

rules.passEvidence: The resume is {n} words, a reasonable length.
rules.failEvidence: The resume is {n} {n|word|words}, outside the range most reviewers expect.
rules.fix: Keep the resume between about 200 and 1,500 words: one or two pages.

bands.failEvidence: The resume is {n} {n|word|words}, too short to show what you did.
bands.fix: Add to it: a few bullets for each recent role saying what you did and what came of it.

bands.failEvidence: The resume is {n} words, too long for a reviewer to read through.
bands.fix: Cut it to what matters for the job: recent roles in full, older ones in a line or two.

rules.passEvidence: Headings extract as whole words.
rules.failEvidence: {n} {n|line extracts|lines extract} with a space between letters, as a heading set as "E X P E R I E N C E" does.
rules.fix: Remove the letter spacing (tracking) from section headings so they extract as words.

rules.passEvidence: {pct}% of content lines carry a number.
rules.failEvidence: Only {pct}% of content lines carry a number.
rules.fix: Quantify outcomes: amounts, percentages, timeframes, headcounts.

rules.passEvidence: {pct}% of bullets name an action you took.
rules.failEvidence: Only {pct}% of bullets name an action you took; the rest read as duties or labels.
rules.fix: Make each bullet say what you did, with an action word ("Led", "Built", "Cut"), rather than what the job was.

rules.passEvidence: Little filler language.
rules.failEvidence: {n} filler {n|phrase was|phrases were} found.
rules.fix: Replace filler phrases with a specific thing you did.

rules.passEvidence: The document reads as a single column.
rules.failEvidence: The document appears to use a multi-column layout.
rules.fix: Use a single-column layout; columns extract in a scrambled order.

rules.passEvidence: No ruled tables were found.
rules.failEvidence: {n} ruled {n|table was|tables were} found.
rules.fix: Replace tables with plain paragraphs and bullets.

rules.passEvidence: The dates in the work history are consistent.
rules.failEvidence: {n} {n|date|dates} in the work history {n|looks|look} wrong: {sample}.
rules.fix: Check the dates: a role cannot start after today, and an end date left off makes jobs overlap.

rules.passEvidence: Most listed skills are backed by the work they were used in.
rules.failEvidence: {pct}% of listed skills appear nowhere but the skills list, such as {sample}.
rules.fix: Name each key skill in the role or project where you used it, not only in the list.

rules.passEvidence: Every page has a text layer.
rules.failEvidence: {n} {n|page is a picture|pages are pictures} with no text, so an ATS reads nothing on {n|it|them}.
rules.fix: Export the resume as a text PDF rather than scanning it or saving it as an image.

rules.passEvidence: No instructions aimed at an AI screener.
rules.failEvidence: An instruction aimed at an AI screener was found: "{sample}".
rules.fix: Remove it. Recruiters and screening tools treat instructions to an AI as manipulation, and many reject the application on sight.

rules.passEvidence: No hidden text.
rules.failEvidence: {n} {n|character is|characters are} hidden from a reader but read by an ATS, starting "{sample}".
rules.fix: Remove hidden text. White or tiny text and text behind an image is read by the ATS and treated as keyword stuffing once a recruiter sees it.

rules.passEvidence: The resume is not a copy of the posting.
rules.failEvidence: {pct}% of the job posting appears word for word in the resume, such as "{sample}".
rules.fix: Describe your own experience. A pasted posting is caught the moment a recruiter reads the resume.

rules.passEvidence: No invisible characters.
rules.failEvidence: {n} invisible {n|character was|characters were} found in the text.
rules.fix: Remove zero-width and other invisible characters; retype any word they split.

rules.passEvidence: No look-alike letters from other alphabets.
rules.failEvidence: {n} {n|word mixes|words mix} Latin with look-alike letters from another alphabet, such as "{sample}".
rules.fix: Retype those words: they look right but no search matches them.

rules.passEvidence: No keyword stuffing.
rules.failEvidence: {n} {n|term or line is|terms or lines are} repeated far beyond what the text needs, such as "{sample}".
rules.fix: Name each skill where you used it. Repetition does not raise a match score in a modern ATS, and recruiters read it as stuffing.

rules.passEvidence: No photo was found.
rules.failEvidence: {n} {n|image was|images were} found, most likely a photo.
rules.fix: Leave the photo off unless the country you are applying in expects one.

rules.passEvidence: {n} {n|role was|roles were} recovered from the work history.
rules.failEvidence: No roles could be recovered from the work history.
rules.fix: Give each job a line with the title, the employer, and a date range.

rules.passEvidence: {pct}% of recovered roles have a title, an employer and a start date.
rules.failEvidence: Only {pct}% of recovered roles are complete.
rules.fix: Make sure every job lists a title, an employer, and a date range.

rules.passEvidence: {pct}% of the expected contact fields were recovered.
rules.failEvidence: Only {pct}% of the expected contact fields were recovered.
rules.fix: Include a name, an email address, and a phone number as plain text.

rules.passEvidence: No date of birth is stated.
rules.failEvidence: A date of birth is stated.
rules.fix: Leave your date of birth off unless the country you are applying in expects it.

rules.passEvidence: No bullet speaks in the first person.
rules.failEvidence: {n} {n|bullet speaks|bullets speak} in the first person, such as "{sample}".
rules.fix: Leave out "I", "my" and "we": open each bullet with what you did ("Led the payments team").

rules.passEvidence: Most bullets are in the active voice.
rules.failEvidence: {pct}% of bullets are in the passive voice, such as "{sample}".
rules.fix: Say who acted: "Rebuilt the payments service in Go", not "The payments service was rebuilt".

rules.passEvidence: Bullets open with an action rather than a duty.
rules.failEvidence: {n} {n|bullet opens|bullets open} with a duty rather than an action, such as "{sample}".
rules.fix: Replace "Responsible for", "Worked on" and the like with the verb for what you did, and say what came of it.

rules.passEvidence: Past roles are written in the past tense.
rules.failEvidence: {n} {n|bullet|bullets} in a past role {n|is|are} in the present tense, such as "{sample}".
rules.fix: Write roles you have left in the past tense ("Led", not "Lead"). The role you hold now can use either.

rules.passEvidence: No bullet runs past two lines.
rules.failEvidence: {n} {n|bullet runs|bullets run} past two lines, such as "{sample}".
rules.fix: Keep each bullet to one or two lines, one action and its result; split a longer one in two.

rules.passEvidence: Each role has a readable number of bullets.
rules.failEvidence: {n} {n|role has|roles have} too few or too many bullets, such as "{sample}".
rules.fix: Give each role two to eight bullets: enough to show what you did, few enough to read.

rules.passEvidence: Bullets in a row open with different words.
rules.failEvidence: {n} {n|run|runs} of three or more bullets in a row {n|opens|open} with the same word, such as "{sample}".
rules.fix: Vary the opening verbs, so each bullet reads as its own result rather than one duty repeated.

rules.passEvidence: Role dates are written one way throughout.
rules.failEvidence: Role dates are written {n} different ways, such as {sample}.
rules.fix: Write every date the same way, such as "Jan 2020 – Mar 2023".

notes.message: Greenhouse documents that it cannot parse a resume larger than 2.5 MB: the file is only attached, and its details are left to be typed in by hand.
Greenhouse lists columns, tables, headers and footers, graphics, and a name or contact details in a header, footer or text box among the causes of a failed or partial parse.
Lever documents that it cannot parse a resume saved as an image (JPG, PNG), and suggests a test: if you cannot select the text in the file, it is likely not parseable.

In Oracle Taleo each employer's administrators choose which file formats candidates may attach, so use one the careers site offers; PDF, Word (.doc, .docx), RTF, HTML and plain text are among those Taleo supports.

fileName.message: The file name does not say whose resume it is, or reads as a draft. Recruiters see it in the ATS and in their downloads, beside everyone else's.

messages.fileNameDraft: The file is named "{name}", which reads as a draft: {marks}.

fileSize.message: The file is larger than {limit}. Many ATS upload forms and parsers stop at about that size; it is a common limit, not a universal one.
fileSize.fix: Shrink or remove the images and export again; a resume of text alone is well under {limit}.

passwordProtected.message: The file is password-protected or encrypted. An ATS that cannot open it reads nothing, and some refuse an encrypted file even when it opens without a password.
passwordProtected.fix: Save a copy with no password or security settings, and upload that.

trackedChanges.message: The document still holds tracked changes. A recruiter who opens it in Word sees the edits, and a parser may read deleted text as if it were there.
trackedChanges.fix: In Word, accept or reject every change (Review, Accept All Changes), turn Track Changes off, and save again.

comments.message: The document still holds comments. A recruiter who opens it in Word sees them.
comments.fix: In Word, delete them (Review, Delete All Comments in Document) and save again.

graduationYear.message: A graduation year more than {years} years back lets a reader work out your age, which can invite age bias. Leaving off graduation years older than about 15 years is common advice; the degree and the school are what a screen checks.
graduationYear.fix: Keep the degree and the school, and leave the year off.

experienceYears.message: More than {years} years of experience, stated or dated in full, lets a reader work out your age, which can invite age bias.
experienceYears.fix: Show the last 15 years or so in detail, sum up earlier roles in a line without dates, and write "15+ years" rather than the full count.

messages.experienceHistory: {n} years of work history are dated.
